takeaway: Tumour suppressor genes: APC chromosome 5, p53 and NF1 chromosome 17, retinoblastoma chromosome 13, WT1 chromosome 11. Only APC with 5 is a correct pair here.

question.text: Which tumour suppressor gene is correctly paired with its chromosome of origin?

lines.text: Tumour suppressor genes are the police of the cell cycle, switching proliferation off in G1.
Both copies must be lost for cancer to develop.
APC sits on chromosome five, and its loss causes colorectal cancer.
p53 and NF1 are on chromosome seventeen, retinoblastoma is on thirteen, and WT1 is on eleven.
So the pairings with p53 on thirteen, retinoblastoma on seventeen, NF1 on eleven or WT1 on seventeen are wrong.
The correct pair is APC, chromosome five.
